title: Where the Dimes band worked; playing for white dances
summary: They played dances around the city and handed overflow jobs to other bands; Vincent describes playing white people's music versus their own.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Where did you work with Wesley Dones?

So where did you work with Wesley Dones? Well, we worked all around the city, until we'd give a dance ourselves with the rest of Baton Rouge. And then we got to play the concert. And after that, the right thing we got traded by the old band. And when they got ready to hire, we had so many dates we couldn't make it. So we'd give it to Bob Lyons. And Bob Lyons sent them 75 dollars deposit. And somehow, they wrote back to us and told him they didn't care for him so much he could keep the money, you know. So they said if we couldn't come, they had to get a band. We told them we couldn't make it so they got that band from Nazi. The Scott Band. You ever heard of that band? Yeah, they got that band. They stayed there about three years. We used to work for all these studios down there all the time. And I hold them all the time, you know. And then all these hotels we used to work in, you know. And dance and all, you know. But I was with wrestling. And then the white people, the white people, they had their own music, you know. And we had our own music too. And we'd go there to give us their music to play. That's where they'd catch us, you see. And we could play their music. But some of the things couldn't play their music, so I started playing his music, you know. Instead of staying, he couldn't hold a band by himself. He had two cornet players. He couldn't make it with one.
Ask him who he would use on second cornet.
